subject.title: doctor --fix migrates codex/gpt-5.5 to openai/gpt-5.5, then Codex app-server startup times out on 2026.6.1

question: Should doctor retain unsafe legacy Codex routes until credentials/runtime/session state are proven safe to canonicalize, and should this issue require the Codex initialize-timeout fix before close?
rationale: Current policy says `openai/*` plus Codex runtime is canonical, but the report shows the migration can create an unusable real setup; deciding whether retained legacy routes are acceptable and whether the startup-timeout repair is part of closure requires maintainer product and upgrade intent.

options.title: Review both candidate tracks before close
options.body: Treat the migration-plan PR and the Codex startup-timeout PR as complementary evidence paths, then close this issue only after the merged behavior covers the reported smoke route or maintainers explicitly narrow the scope.

options.title: Migration policy only
options.body: Accept retained-route doctor behavior as the issue fix and leave Codex startup timeout handling to the separate startup/cron issue cluster.

options.title: Keep canonical migration strict
options.body: Preserve unconditional canonicalization to `openai/*` and require a separate live startup/runtime fix to make migrated routes healthy everywhere.

recommendation.title: Review both candidate tracks before close
recommendation.body: Treat the migration-plan PR and the Codex startup-timeout PR as complementary evidence paths, then close this issue only after the merged behavior covers the reported smoke route or maintainers explicitly narrow the scope.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is around Codex auth/routing and app-server startup ownership, and this decision spans those surfaces.
